title: The window's own lend trips the fresh-record RESERVE rule: on a record with no proven cycle, the second tier opens with no refusal
claim: lj52_gc_reserve (1165-1173) moves a record to RESERVE when no cycle has been proven yet (gc_hyst == 0) and used > total + G/2. That rule was written for eris history. THE WINDOW now lets the sandbox itself take used past total + G/2: lj52_gc_lend (1223-1229) grants up to S + L in BURST. On the next slow-path call, lj52_gc_credit, which runs inside the alloc predicate at 411/478, sees the lent bytes and flips the record to RESERVE, so a credit of G is granted with no refusal at all. This contradicts the BURST comment at 956-959 ('Before any refusal the heap stops at total + G/2 (+ THE WINDOW below, for the sandbox), so when the refusal comes at least G/2 (G/2 - LJ52_GC_LEND) is left'). The first refusal then comes at the ceiling T + G + L, with nothing left for the handler's next allocation: the very failure THE CREDIT was built to prevent. It is the hazard the fresh-record bullet itself names (968-971: 'taking that as a reserve would spend the second tier before any refusal'), now reachable by the sandbox and not only through the kernel's slice. The bound T + G + L is not broken. It only happens on a record with no proven cycle (a state just loaded or created) and needs several growths with no completed checkpoint between them, so it is narrow. Stage C refuses at S here.
evidence: Probe in my scratch dir (review/shim/rv.c, function f1; logs rv-2.log, rv-3.log, rvC-1.log). It uses a fresh record, the sandbox thread (a coroutine resumed under _OCLJ_WATCHDOG.arm), the heap at S - 1 KB, and one lua_createtable(256, 512) from a C function, so no checkpoint runs between the header, array and hash allocations. THE WINDOW object (d1242186), C and legacy alike: 'FRESH ... GRANTED; refusals +0, lends +1, od_state 1, od_peak 29768 = G/2 + 13384 (S + L = G/2 + 4096), hyst 0'. Control, one proof first: 'PROVEN ... refused; refusals +1, od_peak 17480 = G/2 + 1096'. Stage C object, both: 'refused; refusals +1, od_peak = G/2 - 960'. Order of events: the array part is lent past S (win=1). The hash part's credit call then hits !gc_hyst && used > total + G/2 at 1168, takes RESERVE, and the hash part is granted on credit.
fix: Keep the window's lent bytes out of the fresh-record test. For example, guard 1168 with !M->gc_win: it is 0 on a fresh record until a lend opens it, and a refusal opens RESERVE anyway. Alternatively, compare against total + G/2 + LJ52_GC_LEND, or skip the lend while gc_hyst == 0. Add a W11 variant, the probe above: the fresh record must refuse the hash part, not grant it at G/2 + 13 KB.
repro: sh review/shim/mk.sh rv.c <wall2/W/lj52shim-additive.o> rv.exe; affrun 3FC3FC default rv.exe; read the F1 lines. FRESH is granted past S + L with refusals +0, while PROVEN and every stage-C row are refused.

title: The verdict is not sticky: a refusal clears it, so the next crossing is lent with the proof's heap still past S, contradicting the THE WINDOW comment
claim: The comment at 1048-1051 says that on the verdict 'every further crossing is refused while that proof's heap stays past the current S (a raised cap or an opened reserve tier voids it)'. The code refuses exactly one crossing per verdict. The verdict is checked only while gc_win == 2 (1225), and the refusal it causes runs lj52_gc_refused, which sets gc_win = 0 (1246). The proof of the cycle that refusal arms makes no decision, because the window block at 1291 is skipped when gc_win == 0. So the next sandbox crossing is lent (1226-1229), even though that latest proof found the heap past S. Then win=1, the next proof gives the verdict again, one more refusal follows, and so on. A program that catches its refusals and keeps trying therefore gets one in two attempts lent, and climbs to the ceiling S + L. The wording at 1066 is also wrong: 'A refusal shuts the window, so the cycle it arms decides the next crossing'. Whenever that cycle proves before the next crossing, it decides nothing. The d2-final design (§1: 'the next crossing is refused'; §4: REFUSE sets WIN = 0) matches the code, so the comment is what is wrong. The bound is unaffected: it is the ceiling. But the comment misdescribes the verdict as a stop, and W17's 'the window is not a third tier' holds only for a program that stops at its first refusal.
evidence: Probe review/shim/rv.c, function f2, with logs rv-2.log and rv-3.log; stable across runs. The sandbox makes 8000 caught one-table attempts, recording the window's state around each. On THE WINDOW object: 'refused 4604, granted past the top 48; refusals under a standing verdict 42, of which the NEXT attempt was lent past the top with the latest proof's heap still past it: 42'. Trace: attempt 3354 'before win 1, gc_low = S +72, used = S +160 -> REFUSED' (the look's proof gives the verdict). Attempt 3355 'before win 0, gc_low = S +160, used = S +160 -> granted, used after = S +248'. Attempt 3356 is refused again. Peak used = G + 4032, which matches the suite's own W7 od_peak of G + 4078 and W19's 'reached G + 4080'. On stage C the same program never gets past the top (peak G - 16).
fix: Correct the comment. The verdict refuses the next crossing only. The refusal shuts the window (1246) and the cycle it arms judges nothing (1291), so the crossing after a refused one is lent within S + L. A program that catches refusals climbs to the ceiling, one grant per two attempts (W7, W19). If a sticky verdict was intended, a verdict refusal must not clear gc_win. That conflicts with W16Rj, which needs the lend after a refusal, so the comment is the thing to change.
repro: Build rv.c as above against wall2/W/lj52shim-additive.o and run it pinned. In the F2 line, 'NEXT attempt was lent ... still past it' is greater than 0, and the four-attempt trace alternates REFUSED and granted with gc_low > S.

- d2-final.md:526 says REFUSE sets WIN = 0.

title: No test or sabotage covers THE WINDOW on the legacy (dropin) allocator path; W18's 'legacy' runs cannot see it

title: W16 family never asserts 'other' == 0, so kernel refusals (machine downs) during the sweep pass silently
claim: A run whose kernel is refused (st != 0: the per-resume table.pack, which is machine.lua's unprotected pack) or which never records anything is counted as 'other'. The ok() only requires nin > 0 && ncov == 0 (:2205, :2263). So W16, W16R and W16Rj fail on kernel downs only when every one of the 96 runs dies. Any smaller number of downs passes.
evidence: In the negctl run, nokslice/run.log (build/native/negctl/nokslice) shows `PASS W16 ... inside 89, stall 0, sandbox down 0, other 7`: 7 of 96 kernel refusals after the sandbox's refusal, and W16 passes. W16R/W16Rj fail under nokslice only because all 96 runs were 'other' (nin == 0). On the canonical object 'other' is 0 in every W16/W16R/W16Rj line of the 30 final, 10 dropin and 10 stage-C runs (270 lines, scratchpad wall2/W/mt1 and d2-final/out11), so asserting it would cause no false failure.
fix: Add `nother == 0` to the three ok()s. The nokslice expected set then gains W16, and the comment at negative-control.sh 4.10 needs updating to match.

title: W16R/W16Rj judge the tier by the program's own refusal count, which misses refusals the JIT recorder absorbs and undercounts covered landings
claim: topr picks cap+G only when nfail > 0 (w16r_rec, :781). A refusal that trace_abort absorbs silently opens the shim's RESERVE tier but leaves nfail at 0. The next landing outside the handler is then judged against cap+G/2, and a landing that garbage covers under the tier it actually happened in is not counted. The comment's 'judged against the tier it happened in' (:2209-2215 region) does not hold with the JIT on.
evidence: Instrumented copy (review/tests/mem_test_dbg.c, which also records GC_REFUSALS at the record): on stage C, each W16Rj sweep has 6 code-2/3 landings with tier=0 but 2 shim refusals, 5 of them covR=1 covB=0. title: Comment claims the verdict refuses every further crossing; the code refuses one, then lends the next
claim:
Lines 1048-1051 say that at THE VERDICT 'every further crossing is refused while that proof's heap stays past the current S'. The code does something else:
- The first verdict refusal goes through lj52_gc_refused, which sets gc_win = 0 unconditionally for a sandbox thread (:1246). It also opens the reserve tier (:1245).
- The lend refuses only when gc_win == 2 (:1225), so the next crossing within the ceiling is lent and gc_win goes back to 1 (:1226).
So a standing verdict refuses exactly one crossing at a time.
Lines 1066-1067 ('A refusal shuts the window, so the cycle it arms decides the next crossing') are also inaccurate. If the refusal's cycle completes before the next crossing, its proof sees gc_win == 0 and decides nothing (:1291). The next crossing is then lent unconditionally, and only the cycle that lend arms decides.
evidence: lj52shim.c:1225 `if (M->gc_win == 2 && M->gc_low > top) return 0;`; :1246 `M->gc_win = 0;` in lj52_gc_refused; :1291 `if (M->gc_win) { ... }` is the only place a proof decides the window. A refusal also opens the reserve tier at :1245, which voids a burst-tier verdict at once.
fix: Reword. A standing verdict refuses the next crossing. That refusal shuts the window, so the crossing after it is lent within the ceiling, and a later proof decides again. The verdict is also voided by frees that bring gc_low under S, a raised cap, or an opened reserve tier.

check.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and couldn't, either from the code or by running it. The finding is a false comment, not a safety defect.

Code path (C:/Users/astro/Downloads/OC-LuaJIT/native/lj52shim.c):
- The lend refuses because of the verdict only when `M->gc_win == 2 && M->gc_low > top` (:1225). Every other lend within the ceiling sets `gc_win = 1` (:1226).
- A verdict refusal goes through `lj52_gc_refused` (called at :414 and :485), which sets `gc_win = 0` (:1246).
- The guards that skip that reset (HOOK_GC, GCSTOP, norefuse, `L == NULL`) also stop the lend from being reached, or stop it refusing for the verdict. So after a verdict refusal the window is always shut.
- A proof decides the window only inside `if (M->gc_win)` (:1291). A proof that finds the window shut decides nothing.

So a verdict that stays true refuses one crossing, lends the next, and so on alternately. It does not refuse "every further crossing" as the comment at :1048-1051 says. The design itself says the code's version: d2-final.md:29 "the verdict, and the next crossing is refused", :32 "A refusal shuts the window", and the §4 table (REFUSE → WIN = 0). The comment is wrong against both the code and the design.

Reproduction (scratchpad/wall2/review/verify-15/):
- probe.c is mem_test.c's helpers plus a W17-style sandbox driver, linked against lj52shim-additive.o (md5 d1242186), pinned with affrun 3FC3FC.
- Fill 1 is refused in the burst tier, which opens the reserve tier. Fill 2 is refused by the verdict in the reserve tier. Then four single 64-byte table allocations follow, each under pcall.
- In 3/3 runs with JIT off and 1/1 with JIT on, those four went LENT (lends 4→5, win=1), REFUSED, LENT, REFUSED, with the live heap past S the whole time.
- Logs: run-off-1..3.log and run-on-1.log.

The second part of the finding also holds. "A refusal shuts the window, so the cycle it arms decides the next crossing" (:1066-1067) is false in the case the probe hits. At the first allocation after the refusal:
- collects went 30→31: the refusal's cycle was proven, with the window shut, so it decided nothing;
- arms went 31→32: the lend armed its own cycle;
- that new cycle's proof gave the verdict that refused the crossing after.

The refusal's cycle decides the window only when the next crossing comes before that cycle finishes (W16Rj's shape).

Impact: the absolute bound is unaffected. The ceiling at :1224 still caps every lend at S + LJ52_GC_LEND, and the lent objects push the heap up by one object per two crossings, within that ceiling. This is a documentation inaccuracy only, so minor is right.
check.fix:
Reword lj52shim.c:1048-1051 to match the code and d2-final.md:29/32, for example: "past S even without the bytes granted since the PREVIOUS proof, i.e. data that survived two consecutive cycles: THE VERDICT, and the next crossing is refused while that proof's heap stays past the current S (a raised cap or an opened reserve tier voids it). The refusal shuts the window, so the crossing after it is lent within the ceiling and a later proof decides again: a standing verdict refuses every other crossing, never more than LJ52_GC_LEND past S."

Reword :1066-1067 as well: "A refusal shuts the window, so the next crossing is lent within the ceiling and the next proof decides again (the refusal's own cycle when it has not yet run, else the cycle the lend arms): ..."
